420:     def write_segment_byte(self, index: int, value: int, high: bool = False) -> None:
421:         """Anode/segment byte write (pages 0x82 / 0x92 in the RE map).
422: 
423:         The value is only *latched*; the firmware writes both segment bytes and
424:         then the grid select, so the cell is committed by :meth:`select_grid`
425:         (ROM order: 0x92, 0x82, then 0xA2 - see 0x8309..0x831E).
426:         """
427:         self.writes += 1
428:         if high:

430:         else:
431:             self.seg0 = value & 0xFF

435:         """Latch the shared segment byte(s) without touching any digit."""
436:         self.writes += 1

439:         if high is not None:

443:         """Show the latched segments on ``index`` (default: current grid)."""

1: """The cash-register keyboard: an 8x8 scanned matrix.
2: 
3: Evidence from the firmware (see ``docs/hardware_analysis.md``):
4: 
5: * the scan runs inside the multiplex ISR at ROM ``0x838B``-``0x839D``::
6: 
7:       838B  MOV  A,R0
8:       838C  ANL  A,#07h        ; row = scan counter & 7
9:       838E  ORL  A,#30h
10:       8390  MOV  R1,A
11:       8391  MOV  1Ah,@R1       ; previous value, internal RAM 0x30+row
12:       8393  MOV  DPH,#91h
13:       8396  MOV  DPL,A
14:       8398  MOVX A,@DPTR        ; read the column byte of that row
15:       8399  CPL  A              ; columns are ACTIVE LOW
16: 
17: * detected keys are decoded and pushed into a ring buffer in external RAM
18:   (``0x83E0``: ``MOV DPH,#0Ch / MOV DPL,4Fh / MOVX @DPTR,A``) that the main
19:   program pops at ``0xDCD5``; ``CLR EX0`` around that access shows the machine
20:   raises INT0 for a key event.
21: 
22: The board exposes the matrix in two ways, both driving this one object:
23: 
24: * native: read XDATA ``0x9130 + row`` -> column byte (active low);
25: * 8255:   PPI port C -> column byte of the row selected by port B.
26: """
27: 
28: from __future__ import annotations
29: 
30: import threading
31: from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
32: 
33: __all__ = ["Keyboard", "KEYS", "LAYOUT", "ALIASES"]
34: 
35: # Row-major layout of the emulated keyboard, 8 columns per row.
36: # An empty string is a physically unpopulated position.
37: LAYOUT: List[List[str]] = [
38:     ["7", "8", "9", "X", "СУММА", "ОПЛ", "ITOG", "00"],
39:     ["4", "5", "6", "СКИДКА", "ОТМЕНА", "ВОЗВРАТ", "ПОДЫТОГ", "."],
40:     ["1", "2", "3", "КАССИР", "СЕРВИС", "РЕЖИМ", "ВВОД", "СБРОС"],
41:     ["0", "СТРЕЛКА_ВЛЕВО", "СТРЕЛКА_ВПРАВО", "ПРОБЕЛ", "ТАБ", "ЧЕК", "КС", "Z"],
42:     ["ПИТ", "", "", "", "", "", "", ""],
43:     ["", "", "", "", "", "", "", ""],
44:     ["", "", "", "", "", "", "", ""],
45:     ["", "", "", "", "", "", "", ""],
46: ]
47: 
48: # Names accepted by press()/release() even though they are not physical keys.
49: ALIASES: Dict[str, str] = {
50:     "ИТОГ": "ITOG", "СУММ": "СУММА", "ОПЛАТА": "ОПЛ",
51:     "XREPORT": "КС", "ZREPORT": "Z", "FEED": "ПИТ", "RECEIPT": "ЧЕК",
52:     "ENTER": "ВВОД", "CLEAR": "СБРОС", "SUBTOTAL": "ПОДЫТОГ",
53:     "MODE": "РЕЖИМ", "SERVICE": "СЕРВИС", "CASHIER": "КАССИР",
54:     "DISCOUNT": "СКИДКА", "CANCEL": "ОТМЕНА", "PAY": "ОПЛ", "MULT": "X",
55:     "RETURN": "ВОЗВРАТ", "LEFT": "СТРЕЛКА_ВЛЕВО", "RIGHT": "СТРЕЛКА_ВПРАВО",
56:     "SPACE": "ПРОБЕЛ", "TAB": "ТАБ",
57: }
58: 
59: KEYS: List[str] = [name for row in LAYOUT for name in row if name]
60: 
61: 
62: class Keyboard:
63:     """An 8x8 matrix of normally-open contacts to ground.
64: 
65:     ``press`` closes a contact: the column bit of that (row, column) reads
66:     **0** while the row is driven.  Pressing a key that has no physical
67:     position is accepted and remembered so the UI never has to special-case
68:     the layout ("a contact into thin air", as the board contract allows).
69:     """
70: 
71:     rows = 8
72:     cols = 8
73:     #: a momentary tap() keeps the contact closed this many machine cycles
74:     tap_cycles = 40_000
75: 
76:     def __init__(self, layout: Optional[List[List[str]]] = None) -> None:
77:         self._lock = threading.RLock()
78:         self.layout = [list(r) for r in (layout if layout is not None else LAYOUT)]
79:         self._pos: Dict[str, Tuple[int, int]] = {}
80:         for r, row in enumerate(self.layout):
81:             for c, name in enumerate(row):
82:                 if name:
83:                     self._pos.setdefault(name, (r, c))
84:         self.keys: List[str] = [n for row in self.layout for n in row if n]
85:         self._pressed: Dict[str, bool] = {name: False for name in self.keys}
86:         self._loose: Dict[str, bool] = {}
87:         self._tap_until: Dict[str, int] = {}
88:         self.press_count = 0
89:         self.release_count = 0
90:         self.event_count = 0            # the board turns this into INT0
91: 
92:     # ------------------------------------------------------------- positions
93:     @staticmethod
94:     def _canonical(name: str) -> str:
95:         return ALIASES.get(name, name)
96: 
97:     def position(self, name: str) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int]]:
98:         return self._pos.get(self._canonical(name))
99: 
100:     def key_at(self, row: int, col: int) -> str:
101:         try:
102:             return self.layout[row][col]
103:         except IndexError:
104:             return ""
105: 
106:     def row_of(self, name: str) -> Optional[int]:
107:         pos = self.position(name)
108:         return None if pos is None else pos[0]
109: 
110:     def col_of(self, name: str) -> Optional[int]:
111:         pos = self.position(name)
112:         return None if pos is None else pos[1]
113: 
114:     # --------------------------------------------------------------- presses
115:     def press(self, name: str) -> None:
116:         name = self._canonical(name)
117:         with self._lock:
118:             if name in self._pressed:
119:                 was, self._pressed[name] = self._pressed[name], True
120:             else:
121:                 was, self._loose[name] = self._loose.get(name, False), True
122:             if not was:
123:                 self.press_count += 1
124:                 self.event_count += 1
125: 
126:     def release(self, name: str) -> None:
127:         name = self._canonical(name)
128:         with self._lock:
129:             if name in self._pressed:
130:                 was, self._pressed[name] = self._pressed[name], False
131:             else:
132:                 was, self._loose[name] = self._loose.get(name, False), False
133:             if was:
134:                 self.release_count += 1
135:                 self.event_count += 1
136: 
137:     def tap(self, name: str) -> None:
138:         """Momentary press used by mouse clicks.
139: 
140:         The contact stays closed for :attr:`tap_cycles` machine cycles so a
141:         polling firmware cannot miss it; :meth:`tick` re-opens it.
142:         """
143:         self.press(name)
144:         with self._lock:
145:             self._tap_until[name] = self.tap_cycles
146: 
147:     # -------------------------------------------------------------- scanning
148:     def is_pressed(self, name: str) -> bool:
149:         name = self._canonical(name)
150:         with self._lock:
151:             if name in self._pressed:
152:                 return bool(self._pressed[name])
153:             return bool(self._loose.get(name, False))
154: 
155:     def pressed_keys(self) -> List[str]:
156:         with self._lock:
157:             out = [n for n in self.keys if self._pressed.get(n)]
158:             out += [n for n, v in self._loose.items() if v]
159:             return out
160: 
161:     def any_pressed(self) -> bool:
162:         with self._lock:
163:             return any(self._pressed.values()) or any(self._loose.values())
164: 
165:     def read_columns(self, row: int) -> int:
166:         """Column byte for ``row``: bit = 1 idle (pull-up), 0 = contact closed.
167: 
168:         Unpopulated positions are not connected to anything, so they stay high.
169:         """
170:         if row < 0 or row >= self.rows:
171:             return 0xFF
172:         cols = 0
173:         with self._lock:
174:             for c in range(self.cols):
175:                 name = self.key_at(row, c)
176:                 if name and (self._pressed.get(name) or self._loose.get(name, False)):
177:                     cols |= 1 << c
178:         return (~cols) & 0xFF
179: 
180:     def row_bits(self) -> int:
181:         """Bitmap of rows that currently have at least one key down."""
182:         bits = 0
183:         with self._lock:
184:             for name, (r, _c) in self._pos.items():
185:                 if self._pressed.get(name):
186:                     bits |= 1 << r
187:             if any(self._loose.values()):
188:                 bits |= 0xFF
189:         return bits & 0xFF
190: 
191:     def scan(self) -> List[Tuple[int, int, str]]:
192:         """Every closed contact as ``(row, column, name)``."""
193:         out: List[Tuple[int, int, str]] = []
194:         with self._lock:
195:             for name, (r, c) in self._pos.items():
196:                 if self._pressed.get(name):
197:                     out.append((r, c, name))
198:         return sorted(out)
199: 
200:     # ------------------------------------------------------------------ time
201:     def tick(self, cycles: int) -> None:
202:         """Expire momentary taps so a mouse click behaves like a real press."""
203:         with self._lock:
204:             if not self._tap_until:
205:                 return
206:             for name in list(self._tap_until):
207:                 left = self._tap_until[name] - cycles
208:                 if left <= 0:
209:                     del self._tap_until[name]
210:                     if name in self._pressed:
211:                         self._pressed[name] = False
212:                     else:
213:                         self._loose[name] = False
214:                 else:
215:                     self._tap_until[name] = left
216: 
217:     def clear(self) -> None:
218:         with self._lock:
219:             for n in self._pressed:
220:                 self._pressed[n] = False
221:             for n in self._loose:
222:                 self._loose[n] = False
223:             self._tap_until.clear()
224: 
225:     def describe(self) -> str:
226:         down = self.pressed_keys()
227:         return f"keyboard {self.rows}x{self.cols}, down={down or '-'}"
228: 
229:     def __repr__(self) -> str:      # pragma: no cover - debugging aid
230:         return f"Keyboard(keys={len(self.keys)}, down={self.pressed_keys()})"

1: """Hardware model of the AO "ETIM" cash register, assembled on an 8051 bus.
2: 
3: Every pin assignment lives in the :data:`WIRING` block below so it can be
4: retuned in one place.  The defaults come from the reverse engineering in
5: ``docs/hardware_analysis.md`` and ``docs/hardware_from_pseudocode.md``; each
6: entry is marked CONFIRMED (quoted ROM/C evidence), HYPOTHESIS (best guess) or
7: DEMO (an interface the board offers for the demo firmware).
8: 
9: External (``MOVX``) map
10: -----------------------
11: ===============  =====================================================
12: address          device
13: ===============  =====================================================
14: 0x0000-0x0003    8255 PPI window 1: PA, PB, PC, CTRL      (HYPOTHESIS)
15: 0x0008-0x000B    8255 PPI window 2 (mirror, same chip)    (HYPOTHESIS)
16: 0x0000-0x7FFF    external RAM (data + key ring buffer)
17: 0x8100-0x81FF    printer data latch (native path)
18: 0x8200-0x82FF    display segment byte 0 (7 segments + dp)
19: 0x9100-0x91FF    keyboard column read, row = low 3 bits of the address
20: 0x9200-0x92FF    display segment byte 1 (extra segments)
21: 0xA100-0xA1FF    display digit/annunciator byte (digit = low 3 bits)
22: 0xA200-0xA2FF    display grid select (0..7 active, 8 = blank)
23: 0xB100-0xB1FF    printer/aux motor phase latch (0x0F / 0x0E)
24: ===============  =====================================================
25: """
26: 
27: from __future__ import annotations
28: 
29: import collections
30: import threading
31: from typing import Deque, Dict, List, Optional
32: 
33: from m8051.bus import (
34:     HardwareBus,
35:     IRQ_INT0,
36:     IRQ_INT1,
37:     IRQ_RX,
38:     IRQ_T0,
39:     IRQ_T1,
40:     IRQ_TX,
41: )
42: 
43: from board.display import SEG7, Display
44: from board.keyboard import Keyboard
45: from board.ppi8255 import CTRL, PORT_A, PORT_B, PORT_C, PPI8255
46: from board.printer import ReceiptPrinter, encode_text
47: 
48: __all__ = ["CashRegisterBoard", "WIRING"]
49: 
50: 
51: # ==========================================================================
52: #  W I R I N G   B L O C K
53: #  Single source of truth for every address, page and bit the board decodes.
54: #  Retune here; nothing below this block hard-codes a pin.
55: # ==========================================================================
56: WIRING: Dict[str, object] = {
57:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------- 8255
58:     # The only *quoted* evidence is
59:     #   FUN_CODE_b469: DAT_EXTMEM_0009 = 0x89; ... DAT_EXTMEM_0009 = 0xa9;
60:     #   FUN_CODE_b274: DAT_EXTMEM_000b = 0x89; ... DAT_EXTMEM_000b = 0xa9;
61:     # and the ROM bytes 0xB27A..0xB281 = 74 89 30 3C 02 74 A9 F3
62:     # (MOV A,#89h / JNB 3Ch,+2 / MOV A,#0A9h / MOVX @R1,A) which are 8255
63:     # mode-set words.  The register base is a HYPOTHESIS: docs/architecture.md
64:     # says 0x0000..0x0003, the firmware writes through R1 = 0x0B with P2
65:     # unresolved, so both windows are decoded onto one PPI.
66:     "PPI_BASE": 0x0000,                 # HYPOTHESIS (docs/architecture.md)
67:     "PPI_MIRROR_BASES": (0x0008,),      # HYPOTHESIS (R1 = 0x0B in ROM)
68:     "PPI_MODE_WORD_DISPLAY": 0x89,      # C L1109/L850 - group A mode 0
69:     "PPI_MODE_WORD_PRINTER": 0xA9,      # C L1111/L852 - group A mode 1
70:     "PPI_A_MEANING": "segments",        # DEMO: "segments" (7-seg mask) | "chars"
71:     "PPI_B_MEANING": "onehot",          # DEMO: "onehot" (bit i) | "binary"
72:     "PPI_C_IS_KEYBOARD": True,          # DEMO: port C = column byte
73: 
74:     # ------------------------------------------------------- display (native)
75:     # CONFIRMED: ROM 0x8309..0x831E
76:     #   830F MOV DPH,#92h / 8312 MOVX @DPTR,A   (segment byte 1)
77:     #   8314 MOV DPH,#82h / 8317 MOVX @DPTR,A   (segment byte 0)
78:     #   8319 ANL A,#07h / 831B MOV DPH,#0A2h / 831E MOVX @DPTR,A (grid)
79:     #   C L611: FUN_CODE_810f(*(byte *)((param_2 + 0x1c) + 0x824a) | ...)
80:     "DISPLAY_SEG0_PAGE": 0x82,
81:     "DISPLAY_SEG1_PAGE": 0x92,
82:     "DISPLAY_GRID_PAGE": 0xA2,
83:     "DISPLAY_GRID_BLANK": 0x08,         # ROM 0x82E1: MOV A,#08h -> 0xA2
84:     "DISPLAY_DIGIT_PAGE": 0xA1,         # FUN_CODE_810f: CONCAT11(0xa1,index)
85:     "DISPLAY_DIGITS": 8,                # param_3 clamped 0..7 (C L411-419)
86:     "DISPLAY_LINES": 1,
87:     # ROM 0x8266 holds "AIHLDFBC" = 0x41 0x49 0x48 0x4C 0x44 0x46 0x42 0x43,
88:     # i.e. 0x40 | gray(i): a *selector*, not a segment pattern.
89:     "DISPLAY_A1_GRAY_IS_LAMP": True,
90:     "SEGMENT_ROM_TABLE": 0x8266,        # digit-select/segment table found in ROM
91: 
92:     # ------------------------------------------------------ keyboard (native)
93:     # CONFIRMED: ROM 0x838B..0x8398 - row = R0 & 7, read MOVX from DPH:R1
94:     # with the row in the low address byte and active-low columns (CPL A).
95:     "KEYBOARD_READ_PAGE": 0x91,
96:     "KEYBOARD_READ_BASE": 0x9130,       # low byte = row index (0..7)
97:     "KEYBOARD_ROWS": 8,
98:     "KEYBOARD_COLS": 8,
99:     "KEYBOARD_ACTIVE_LOW": True,
100: 
101:     # ------------------------------------------------------- printer (native)
102:     # CONFIRMED: ROM 0x81F3 MOV DPH,#81h / 0x81F6 MOVX @DPTR,A  then
103:     # 0x81F7 SETB P3.4; released by 0x83F8 CLR P3.4 in the ISR epilogue
104:     # (C L618-626: FUN_CODE_83f0 { EA = 1; T0 = 0; } where Ghidra's T0 = P3.4).
105:     "PRINTER_DATA_PAGE": 0x81,
106:     "PRINTER_DATA_IS_DOTS": False,      # DEMO: native path sends character bytes
107:     "PRINTER_STROBE_PORT": 3,
108:     "PRINTER_STROBE_BIT": 4,            # P3.4, active high pulse
109:     "PRINTER_BUSY_PORT": 1,
110:     "PRINTER_BUSY_BIT": 3,              # P1.3 low = ready (HYPOTHESIS)
111:     "PRINTER_BUSY_ACTIVE_LOW": True,
112:     "PRINTER_COLUMNS": 40,
113:     "PRINTER_BUSY_CYCLES": 0,           # never wedge the firmware
114: 
115:     # --------------------------------------------------------- other devices
116:     "MOTOR_PAGE": 0xB1,                 # ROM 0x840D/0x841A write 0x0F / 0x0E
117:     "MOTOR_PHASES": (0x0F, 0x0E),       # HYPOTHESIS: stepper/carriage phases
118:     "RAM_LIMIT": 0x8000,                # XDATA below this is plain RAM
119:     "KEY_RING_LO": 0x0C80,              # ROM 0x83E0 key ring buffer
120:     "KEY_RING_HI": 0x0C9F,
121:     "RTC_BASE": 0x0CB0,                 # ROM 0x832B: sec/min/hour, BCD
122: 
123:     # ------------------------------------------------------------ senses
124:     # C L464: cVar1 = P1_3; if (cVar1 != '\0') { ... TCON &= 0x3f; ET1 = 0; }
125:     "KEY_PRESENT_PORT": 1,
126:     "KEY_PRESENT_BIT": 3,               # P1.3, active high
127:     "KEY_PRESENT_ACTIVE_HIGH": True,
128: 
129:     # -------------------------------------------------------- interrupts
130:     # CONFIRMED pattern: 0xDCD5 CLR EX0 / 0xDCE4 CJNE A,#0A0h around the key
131:     # ring buffer -> INT0 signals a key event.
132:     "INT0_ON_KEYPRESS": True,
133:     "INT0_HOLD_CYCLES": 2_000,
134:     "EXTRA_IRQ": 0,
135: }
136: 
137: # handy named pages derived from the wiring block
138: _PPI_CTRL_ALIASES = tuple(
139:     [WIRING["PPI_BASE"] + CTRL]                                  # type: ignore[operator]
140:     + [b + CTRL for b in WIRING["PPI_MIRROR_BASES"]]            # type: ignore[union-attr]
141: )
142: #: every external address that decodes to an 8255 register (both windows,
143: #: including the control register), same PPI object.
144: _PPI_ALIASES: Dict[int, int] = {}
145: for _base in (WIRING["PPI_BASE"],) + tuple(WIRING["PPI_MIRROR_BASES"]):   # type: ignore[arg-type]
146:     for _reg in (PORT_A, PORT_B, PORT_C, CTRL):
147:         _PPI_ALIASES[_base + _reg] = _reg
148: _PPI_READ_ALIASES = _PPI_ALIASES

151: class CashRegisterBoard(HardwareBus):
152:     """The whole machine: PPI + display + keyboard + printer, on one bus.
153: 
154:     Thread safety
155:     -------------
156:     ``main.py`` runs the CPU on a daemon thread while Tk calls
157:     :meth:`Keyboard.tap` and reads ``display.text()`` / ``printer.paper()``.
158:     Every entry point here takes :attr:`_lock` (a re-entrant lock) and the
159:     :class:`~board.display.Display` has its own lock, so a key pressed from the
160:     GUI thread is visible to the very next port scan and string snapshots are
161:     consistent.
162:     """
163: 
164:     def __init__(
165:         self,
166:         display: Optional[Display] = None,
167:         keyboard: Optional[Keyboard] = None,
168:         printer: Optional[ReceiptPrinter] = None,
169:         wiring: Optional[Dict[str, object]] = None,
170:         self_test: bool = False,
171:         cpu=None,
172:     ) -> None:
173:         self._lock = threading.RLock()
174:         self.wiring: Dict[str, object] = dict(WIRING)
175:         if wiring:
176:             self.wiring.update(wiring)
177: 
178:         self.display = display or Display(
179:             int(self.wiring["DISPLAY_DIGITS"]), int(self.wiring["DISPLAY_LINES"]))
180:         self.keyboard = keyboard or Keyboard()
181:         self.printer = printer or ReceiptPrinter(
182:             columns=int(self.wiring["PRINTER_COLUMNS"]),
183:             busy_cycles=int(self.wiring["PRINTER_BUSY_CYCLES"]),
184:         )
185:         self.ppi = PPI8255("main")
186: 
187:         # external RAM (0x0000 .. RAM_LIMIT-1) - sparse, reads back 0xFF
188:         self.ram: Dict[int, int] = {}
189:         self.ext: Dict[int, int] = {}          # unmapped-but-observed addresses
190: 
191:         self.cycles = 0
192:         self._cpu = cpu
193:         self._last_pc = 0
194:         self.source = "reset"
195:         self.motor = 0x00
196:         self.print_latch = 0x00
197:         self._print_pending = False
198:         self.busy = False
199:         self._busy_until = 0
200:         self._int0_hold = 0
201:         self._seen_events = self.keyboard.event_count
202:         self._port_latch = [0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF]
203:         # "A" = the firmware writes display data before the digit select,
204:         # "B" = digit select first.  Latched from the first display event.
205:         self._ppi_order: Optional[str] = None
206:         self.serial_out: Deque[int] = collections.deque(maxlen=4096)
207:         self.serial_in: Deque[int] = collections.deque()
208:         self.writes: List[tuple] = []
209:         self.trace_limit = 4096
210: 
211:         # PPI port A/B/C are outputs for the demo firmware's mode word; the
212:         # keyboard drives port C pins.
213:         self._refresh_ppi_pins()
214: 
215:         if self_test:
216:             self.run_self_test()
217: 
218:     # ================================================================= time
219:     def tick(self, cycles: int) -> None:
220:         with self._lock:
221:             self.cycles += int(cycles)
222:             self.printer.tick(cycles)
223:             self.keyboard.tick(cycles)
224:             if self._int0_hold > 0:
225:                 self._int0_hold = max(0, self._int0_hold - int(cycles))
226:             if self._busy_until and self.cycles >= self._busy_until:
227:                 self.busy = False
228: 
229:     def note_pc(self, pc: int) -> None:
230:         """Cheap hook so :meth:`status` can report the CPU's PC."""
231:         self._last_pc = int(pc) & 0xFFFF
232: 
233:     def attach_cpu(self, cpu) -> None:
234:         self._cpu = cpu
235: 
236:     # ====================================================== external memory
237:     def _is_ppi(self, addr: int) -> Optional[int]:
238:         if addr in _PPI_READ_ALIASES:
239:             return _PPI_READ_ALIASES[addr]
240:         return None
241: 
242:     def ext_write(self, addr: int, value: int) -> None:
243:         addr &= 0xFFFF
244:         value &= 0xFF
245:         with self._lock:
246:             self._record(addr, value, "w")
247:             reg = self._is_ppi(addr)
248:             if reg is not None:
249:                 self.ppi.write(reg, value)
250:                 if reg == PORT_A:
251:                     self._ppi_port_a(value)
252:                 elif reg == PORT_B:
253:                     self._ppi_port_b(value)
254:                 elif reg == PORT_C:
255:                     self._refresh_ppi_pins()
256:                 return
257: 
258:             page = addr >> 8
259:             low = addr & 0xFF
260:             if addr < int(self.wiring["RAM_LIMIT"]):
261:                 self.ram[addr] = value
262:                 return
263:             if page == self.wiring["DISPLAY_SEG0_PAGE"]:
264:                 self.display.latch_segments(low=value, high=None)
265:             elif page == self.wiring["DISPLAY_SEG1_PAGE"]:
266:                 self.display.latch_segments(low=None, high=value)
267:             elif page == self.wiring["DISPLAY_GRID_PAGE"]:
268:                 # ROM 0x831B: MOV DPH,#0A2h ; MOVX @DPTR,A - the *data* byte is
269:                 # the grid number (R0 & 7), not the address low byte.
270:                 self.display.select_grid(value, commit=True)
271:             elif page == self.wiring["DISPLAY_DIGIT_PAGE"]:
272:                 self.display.write_digit_byte(low & 0x07, value)
273:             elif page == self.wiring["PRINTER_DATA_PAGE"]:
274:                 self.print_latch = value
275:                 self._print_pending = True
276:                 if self.wiring["PRINTER_DATA_IS_DOTS"]:
277:                     self.printer.write_column(value)
278:             elif page == self.wiring["MOTOR_PAGE"]:
279:                 self.motor = value
280:             elif page == self.wiring["KEYBOARD_READ_PAGE"]:
281:                 pass                       # write-only decode, nothing latched
282:             else:
283:                 self.ext[addr] = value
284: 
285:     def ext_read(self, addr: int, code: bool = False) -> int:
286:         addr &= 0xFFFF
287:         with self._lock:
288:             reg = self._is_ppi(addr)
289:             if reg is not None:
290:                 self._refresh_ppi_pins()
291:                 if reg == PORT_C:
292:                     return self._read_port_c()
293:                 return self.ppi.read(reg)
294:             if addr < int(self.wiring["RAM_LIMIT"]):
295:                 return self.ram.get(addr, 0xFF)
296:             page = addr >> 8
297:             low = addr & 0xFF
298:             key_page = self.wiring["KEYBOARD_READ_PAGE"]
299:             if page == key_page:
300:                 row = (low - (int(self.wiring["KEYBOARD_READ_BASE"]) & 0xFF)) & 0xFF
301:                 if int(self.wiring["KEYBOARD_READ_BASE"]) >> 8 != page:
302:                     row = low
303:                 return self.keyboard.read_columns(row & 0x07)
304:             if page == self.wiring["DISPLAY_DIGIT_PAGE"]:
305:                 return self.display.lamp_readback()
306:             if page == self.wiring["DISPLAY_SEG0_PAGE"]:
307:                 return self.display.seg0
308:             if page == self.wiring["DISPLAY_SEG1_PAGE"]:
309:                 return self.display.seg1
310:             if page == self.wiring["PRINTER_DATA_PAGE"]:
311:                 return self.print_latch
312:             if page == self.wiring["MOTOR_PAGE"]:
313:                 return self.motor
314:             return self.ext.get(addr, 0xFF)
315: 
316:     def ext_probe(self, addr: int) -> bool:
317:         addr &= 0xFFFF
318:         if self._is_ppi(addr) is not None:
319:             return True
320:         return addr >= int(self.wiring["RAM_LIMIT"])
321: 
322:     # ============================================================== PPI paths
323:     def _ppi_port_a(self, value: int) -> None:
324:         """Port A: display segments (mode 0) or a printer byte (mode 1).
325: 
326:         The display is written "digit select first, then data" (order B) or
327:         "data first, then digit select" (order A).  The order is latched from
328:         the very first display event of the session, after which both orders
329:         produce an exact per-digit frame buffer.
330:         """
331:         if self.ppi.mode_a == 1 and not self.ppi.ddr[PORT_A]:
332:             self.printer.write_byte(value)
333:             self.print_latch = value
334:             self.ppi.notify_ack(PORT_A)
335:             self.ppi.clear_intr(PORT_A)
336:             return
337:         if self._ppi_order is None:
338:             self._ppi_order = "A"
339:         if self.wiring["PPI_A_MEANING"] == "chars":
340:             idx = self._ppi_digit()
341:             if idx >= 0:
342:                 self.display.write_char(idx, value)
343:             return
344:         self.display.latch_segments(value, None)
345:         if self._ppi_order == "B":
346:             self.display.commit_grid()
347: 
348:     def _ppi_port_b(self, value: int) -> None:
349:         if self._ppi_order is None:
350:             self._ppi_order = "B"
351:         idx = self._ppi_digit(value)
352:         if idx < 0:
353:             self.display.select_grid(int(self.wiring["DISPLAY_GRID_BLANK"]), commit=False)
354:             return
355:         self.display.select_grid(idx, commit=(self._ppi_order == "A"))
356: 
357:     def _ppi_digit(self, value: Optional[int] = None) -> int:
358:         """Digit index selected by PPI port B (one-hot or binary)."""
359:         if value is None:
360:             value = self.ppi.latch[PORT_B] & 0xFF
361:             # in mode 1 there is no digit select on port B; keep the last one
362:             if self.ppi.mode_b == 1:
363:                 return self.display.grid if self.display.grid is not None else -1
364:         if self.wiring["PPI_B_MEANING"] == "binary":
365:             idx = value & 0x0F
366:         elif value == 0:
367:             return -1
368:         else:
369:             idx = -1
370:             for bit in range(8):
371:                 if value & (1 << bit):
372:                     idx = bit
373:                     break
374:         if idx < 0 or idx >= self.display.digits:
375:             return -1
376:         return idx
377: 
378:     def _refresh_ppi_pins(self) -> None:
379:         """Drive the PPI's port C pins from the keyboard columns."""
380:         if not self.wiring["PPI_C_IS_KEYBOARD"]:
381:             return
382:         row = self.display.grid if self.display.grid >= 0 else 0
383:         self.ppi.set_pins(PORT_C, self.keyboard.read_columns(row))
384: 
385:     def _read_port_c(self) -> int:
386:         """Port C = keyboard columns, except where the PPI owns the pin.
387: 
388:         In mode 0 every bit that is programmed as an input sees the matrix
389:         (the firmware writes 0x89: "A out, B out, C in").  In mode 1/2 the
390:         handshake pins belong to the printer, so they keep the 8255 status
391:         value and the remaining pins stay on the keyboard.
392:         """
393:         row = self.display.grid if self.display.grid >= 0 else 0
394:         cols = self.keyboard.read_columns(row)
395:         if self.ppi.mode_a in (1, 2) or self.ppi.mode_b == 1:
396:             status = self.ppi.read(PORT_C)
397:             claimed = 0xC0 | (0x08 if self.ppi.mode_a in (1, 2) else 0)
398:             if self.ppi.mode_b == 1:
399:                 claimed |= 0x07
400:             return (status & claimed) | (cols & ~claimed & 0xFF)
401:         mask = self.ppi.ddr[PORT_C]              # 1 = input
402:         return (self.ppi.latch[PORT_C] & ~mask & 0xFF) | (cols & mask)
403: 
404:     # ============================================================== ports
405:     def port_read(self, port: int) -> int:
406:         with self._lock:
407:             value = 0xFF
408:             if port == self.wiring["KEY_PRESENT_PORT"]:
409:                 bit = int(self.wiring["KEY_PRESENT_BIT"])
410:                 present = self.keyboard.any_pressed()
411:                 if not self.wiring["KEY_PRESENT_ACTIVE_HIGH"]:
412:                     present = not present
413:                 if present:
414:                     value |= 1 << bit
415:                 else:
416:                     value &= ~(1 << bit) & 0xFF
417:             if port == self.wiring["PRINTER_BUSY_PORT"]:
418:                 bit = int(self.wiring["PRINTER_BUSY_BIT"])
419:                 busy = self.busy or self.printer.is_busy()
420:                 if self.wiring["PRINTER_BUSY_ACTIVE_LOW"]:
421:                     if busy:
422:                         value &= ~(1 << bit) & 0xFF
423:                 elif busy:
424:                     value |= 1 << bit
425:             return value & 0xFF
426: 
427:     def port_write(self, port: int, value: int) -> None:
428:         with self._lock:
429:             old = self._port_latch[port & 3]
430:             self._port_latch[port & 3] = value & 0xFF
431:             self.port_change(port & 3, old, value & 0xFF)
432: 
433:     def port_change(self, port: int, old: int, new: int) -> None:
434:         """Strobe edges.  NOTE: m8051/cpu.py calls port_write() only, so the
435:         board has to do its own edge detection here as well."""
436:         with self._lock:
437:             if port == int(self.wiring["PRINTER_STROBE_PORT"]):
438:                 bit = int(self.wiring["PRINTER_STROBE_BIT"])
439:                 was = (old >> bit) & 1
440:                 now = (new >> bit) & 1
441:                 # ROM 0x81F6/0x81F7: data byte, then SETB P3.4.  A strobe is
442:                 # either a rising edge or the first time the line is raised
443:                 # after fresh data was latched.
444:                 if now and (not was or self._print_pending):
445:                     self._print_pending = False
446:                     if self.wiring["PRINTER_DATA_IS_DOTS"]:
447:                         self.printer.write_column(self.print_latch)
448:                     else:
449:                         self.printer.write_byte(self.print_latch)
450:                     self.ppi.notify_ack(PORT_A)
451: 
452:     # ============================================================ interrupts
453:     def irq_requested(self) -> int:
454:         with self._lock:
455:             mask = 0
456:             if (self.wiring["INT0_ON_KEYPRESS"]
457:                     and self.keyboard.event_count != self._seen_events):
458:                 self._seen_events = self.keyboard.event_count
459:                 self._int0_hold = int(self.wiring["INT0_HOLD_CYCLES"])
460:             if self._int0_hold > 0:
461:                 mask |= IRQ_INT0
462:             mask |= int(self.wiring["EXTRA_IRQ"])
463:             return mask
464: 
465:     # ================================================================ serial
466:     def serial_write(self, byte: int) -> None:
467:         with self._lock:
468:             self.serial_out.append(byte & 0xFF)
469: 
470:     def serial_read(self) -> Optional[int]:
471:         with self._lock:
472:             return self.serial_in.popleft() if self.serial_in else None
473: 
474:     def serial_available(self) -> bool:
475:         with self._lock:
476:             return bool(self.serial_in)
477: 
478:     def feed_serial(self, data) -> None:
479:         """Test/UI hook: bytes the UART will receive."""
480:         with self._lock:
481:             for b in data:
482:                 self.serial_in.append(int(b) & 0xFF)
483: 
484:     # ============================================================ self test
485:     def run_self_test(self) -> None:
486:         """Drive the *real* port interface so the emulated hardware is visible.
487: 
488:         Everything below goes through :meth:`ext_write`, i.e. exactly the path
489:         the CPU uses; nothing pokes ``display``/``printer`` directly.  Only run
490:         when explicitly requested (``CashRegisterBoard(self_test=True)``) so
491:         nothing is faked silently.
492:         """
493:         with self._lock:
494:             self.source = "self-test"
495:             base = int(self.wiring["PPI_BASE"])
496:             seg0 = int(self.wiring["DISPLAY_SEG0_PAGE"]) << 8
497:             grid = int(self.wiring["DISPLAY_GRID_PAGE"]) << 8
498:             prn = int(self.wiring["PRINTER_DATA_PAGE"]) << 8
499:             ctrl = base + CTRL
500: 
501:             self.ext_write(ctrl, int(self.wiring["PPI_MODE_WORD_DISPLAY"]))
502:             self.ext_write(seg0, 0)
503:             self.ext_write(grid, int(self.wiring["DISPLAY_GRID_BLANK"]))
504:             # digits only: a 7-segment font cannot render M/W/T faithfully
505:             for i, ch in enumerate("12345678"):
506:                 if i >= self.display.digits:
507:                     break
508:                 self.ext_write(base + PORT_A, SEG7.get(ch, 0x00))
509:                 self.ext_write(base + PORT_B, 1 << i)
510:             self.ext_write(seg0, 0)
511: 
512:             self.ext_write(ctrl, int(self.wiring["PPI_MODE_WORD_PRINTER"]))
513:             for line in ("КАССА",
514:                          "--------------------",
515:                          "1 Х 12.34      12.34",
516:                          "ИТОГ           12.34",
517:                          "СКИДКА 0%  БЕЗНАЛИЧН",
518:                          "--------------------",
519:                          "СПАСИБО!"):
520:                 for b in encode_text(line + "\n"):
521:                     self.ext_write(base + PORT_A, b)
522:             self.ext_write(ctrl, int(self.wiring["PPI_MODE_WORD_DISPLAY"]))
523:             self.ext_write(prn, 0)
524:             self.source = "self-test"
525: 
526:     # ========================================================= diagnostics
527:     def _record(self, addr: int, value: int, kind: str) -> None:
528:         self.writes.append((self.cycles, kind, addr, value))
529:         if len(self.writes) > self.trace_limit:
530:             del self.writes[: len(self.writes) - self.trace_limit]
531: 
532:     def status(self) -> Dict[str, object]:
533:         """State for the UI status bar (contract extension, optional)."""
534:         with self._lock:
535:             pc = self._last_pc
536:             if self._cpu is not None:
537:                 try:
538:                     pc = int(self._cpu.pc) & 0xFFFF
539:                 except Exception:            # pragma: no cover - CPU not ready
540:                     pc = self._last_pc
541:             return {
542:                 "cycles": int(self.cycles),
543:                 "pc": pc,
544:                 "source": self.source,
545:                 "ppi": self.ppi.control,
546:                 "ppi_mode_a": self.ppi.mode_a,
547:                 "grid": self.display.grid,
548:                 "keys": self.keyboard.pressed_keys(),
549:                 "printer_lines": len(self.printer.paper()),
550:                 "motor": self.motor,
551:                 "serial_out": len(self.serial_out),
552:                 "ram_writes": len(self.ram),
553:                 "text": self.display.text(),
554:             }
555: 
556:     def status_text(self) -> str:
557:         st = self.status()
558:         return (f"{st['source']} cyc={st['cycles']} pc={st['pc']:04X} "
559:                 f"PPI=0x{st['ppi']:02X} grid={st['grid']} "
560:                 f"'{st['text']}' keys={','.join(st['keys']) or '-'}")
561: 
562:     def describe(self) -> str:
563:         with self._lock:
564:             return (f"CashRegisterBoard: {self.display.describe()}; "
565:                     f"{self.keyboard.describe()}; {self.printer.describe()}; "
566:                     f"{self.ppi.describe()}")
567: 
568:     def reset(self) -> None:
569:         with self._lock:
570:             self.ppi.reset()
571:             self.display.clear()
572:             self.printer.clear()
573:             self.keyboard.clear()
574:             self.ram.clear()
575:             self.ext.clear()
576:             self.motor = 0
577:             self.print_latch = 0
578:             self._int0_hold = 0
579:             self._seen_events = self.keyboard.event_count
580:             self._port_latch = [0xFF] * 4
581:             self.source = "reset"

Every pin assignment lives in the :data:`WIRING` block below so it can be
retuned in one place.  The defaults come from the reverse engineering in
entry is marked CONFIRMED (quoted ROM/C evidence), HYPOTHESIS (best guess) or

{"file_path":"C:\Проекты VS\C проги и пай клиенты\test1\test\firmware\demo\cashier.asm","new_string":"SD_DRAW:
        MOV  R0, #(DISP_BUF+MODE_CELL+1) ; денежное поле -- знакоместа 1..7
        MOV  R2, #FIELD_W
        LCALL DRAW_MONEY
        ; индикатор режима -- в свободном знакоместе 0
        MOV  A, MODE
        MOV  DPTR, #DIGIT_SEG
        MOVC A, @A+DPTR
        MOV  DISP_BUF+MODE_CELL, A
        RET

;  DRAW_MONEY: R1 = BCD, R0 = первое знакоместо поля, R2 = ширина поля.
;  Разряды 6..0 (7 цифр) выравниваются по правому краю поля, точка -- на
;  знакоместе разряда единиц рублей (DIGIDX = 2), т.е. ПЕРЕД копейками.
;  Поле затирается ЦЕЛИКОМ, а позиция каждой цифры считается от УЖЕ
;  сдвинутой базы (DMBASE = R0 + ширина - 7), поэтому вызывающая программа
;  не обязана знать ширину: SET_DISPLAY просит ровно FIELD_W знакомест
;  начиная с MODE_CELL+1.  Нули перед числом гасятся, копейки видны всегда.
DRAW_MONEY:
        MOV  A, R0
        ADD  A, R2
        CLR  C
        SUBB A, #7                      ; база = начало поля + ширина - 7
        MOV  DMBASE, A
        MOV  A, R2
        MOV  DMWID, A
        ; --- погасить поле целиком ---
        MOV  A, DMWID
        MOV  R2, A
        MOV  A, R0
        MOV  R0, A
        CLR  A
DM_B:
        MOV  @R0, A
        INC  R0
        DJNZ R2, DM_B
        MOV  DMWIDX, #6                 ; от старшего разряда к младшему
DM_L:
        MOV  A, DMWIDX
        LCALL GETDIG
        JNZ  DM_PR
        MOV  A, SIG
        JNZ  DM_PR
        MOV  A, DMWIDX
        CJNE A, #2, DM_NEXT             ; разряд единиц рублей виден всегда
DM_PR:
        MOV  SIG, #1
        MOV  A, DMWIDX
        LCALL GETDIG
        MOV  DPTR, #DIGIT_SEG
        MOVC A, @A+DPTR
        MOV  MASK, A
        MOV  A, DMWIDX
        CJNE A, #2, DM_NODP             ; точка -- перед копейками
        MOV  A, MASK
        ORL  A, #SEG_DP
        MOV  MASK, A
DM_NODP:
        MOV  A, DMWIDX
        ADD  A, DMBASE                  ; знакоместо = база + разряд
        MOV  R0, A
        MOV  A, MASK
        MOV  @R0, A
DM_NEXT:
        MOV  A, DMWIDX
        JZ   DM_DONE
        DEC  DMWIDX
        SJMP DM_L
DM_DONE:
        RET","old_string":"SD_DRAW:
        MOV  R0, #(DISP_BUF+MODE_CELL)
        MOV  R2, #FIELD_W
        LCALL DRAW_MONEY
        ; индикатор режима -- в свободном знакоместе 0
        MOV  A, MODE
        MOV  DPTR, #DIGIT_SEG
        MOVC A, @A+DPTR
        MOV  DISP_BUF+MODE_CELL, A
        RET

;  DRAW_MONEY: R1 = BCD, R0 = первое знакоместо, R2 = ширина поля.
;  Разряды 6..0 (7 цифр) выравниваются по правому краю; точка -- перед
;  разрядом 1. Знакоместо 0 при ширине 8 остаётся свободным под режим.
DRAW_MONEY:
        MOV  DMBASE, R0
        MOV  DMWID, R2
        MOV  A, R0
        MOV  R0, A
        MOV  R2, DMWID
        CLR  A
DM_B:
        MOV  @R0, A                     ; погасить поле
        INC  R0
        DJNZ R2, DM_B
        MOV  DIGIDX, #6                 ; от старшего разряда к младшему: нули
        MOV  SIG, #0                    ; перед числом гасятся, а разряды копеек
DM_L:                                   ; (1 и 0) видны всегда
        MOV  A, DIGIDX
        LCALL GETDIG
        JNZ  DM_PR
        MOV  A, SIG
        JNZ  DM_PR
        MOV  A, DIGIDX
        CJNE A, #2, DM_NEXT             ; разряд единиц рублей виден всегда
DM_PR:
        MOV  SIG, #1
        MOV  A, DIGIDX
        LCALL GETDIG
        MOV  DPTR, #DIGIT_SEG
        MOVC A, @A+DPTR
        MOV  MASK, A
        MOV  A, DIGIDX
        CJNE A, #2, DM_NODP
        MOV  A, MASK
        ORL  A, #SEG_DP                 ; десятичная точка
        MOV  MASK, A
DM_NODP:
        MOV  A, DMWID
        DEC  A
        CLR  C
        SUBB A, DIGIDX
        ADD  A, DMBASE
        MOV  R0, A
        MOV  @R0, MASK
DM_NEXT:
        MOV  A, DIGIDX
        JZ   DM_DONE
        DEC  DIGIDX
        SJMP DM_L
DM_DONE:
        RET"}

lines.text: ;  SET_DISPLAY: нарисовать то, что соответствует режиму, и индикатор режима.
;    режим 0 -- вводимая сумма,  1 -- итог (мигает индикатор режима),
;  DRAW_MONEY: R1 = BCD, R0 = первое знакоместо, R2 = ширина поля.
;  Разряды 6..0 (7 цифр) выравниваются по правому краю; точка -- перед
;  разрядом 1. Знакоместо 0 при ширине 8 остаётся свободным под режим.
MOV  DIGIDX, #6                 ; от старшего разряда к младшему: нули

        MOV  R0, #(DISP_BUF+MODE_CELL+1) ; денежное поле -- знакоместа MODE_CELL+1..7
        MOV  R2, #FIELD_W
        LCALL DRAW_MONEY
        ; индикатор режима -- в свободном знакоместе 0
        MOV  A, MODE
        MOV  DPTR, #DIGIT_SEG
        MOVC A, @A+DPTR
        MOV  DISP_BUF+MODE_CELL, A
        RET

;  DRAW_MONEY: R1 = BCD, R0 = первое знакоместо поля, R2 = ширина поля.
;  Разряды 6..0 (7 цифр) выравниваются по правому краю поля, точка -- на
;  знакоместе разряда единиц рублей (DIGIDX = 2), т.е. ПЕРЕД копейками.
;  Поле затирается ЦЕЛИКОМ, а знакоместо каждой цифры считается от УЖЕ
;  сдвинутой базы (DMBASE = начало поля + ширина - 7), поэтому вызывающая
;  программа не обязана знать ширину: SET_DISPLAY просит ровно FIELD_W
;  знакомест начиная с MODE_CELL+1, и индикатор режима (знакоместо 0) в
;  поле не попадает.  Нули перед числом гасятся, копейки видны всегда.

        MOV  A, R0
        ADD  A, R2
        CLR  C
        SUBB A, #7                      ; база = начало поля + ширина - 7
        MOV  DMBASE, A
        MOV  A, R2
        MOV  DMWID, A
        ; --- погасить поле целиком ---
        MOV  A, DMWID
        MOV  R2, A
        MOV  A, R0
        MOV  R0, A
        CLR  A
DM_B:
        MOV  @R0, A
        INC  R0
        DJNZ R2, DM_B
        MOV  DMWIDX, #6                 ; от старшего разряда к младшему: нули
        MOV  SIG, #0                    ; перед числом гасятся, а разряды копеек
DM_L:                                   ; (1 и 0) видны всегда
        MOV  A, DMWIDX
        LCALL GETDIG
        JNZ  DM_PR
        MOV  A, SIG
        JNZ  DM_PR
        MOV  A, DMWIDX
        CJNE A, #2, DM_NEXT             ; разряд единиц рублей виден всегда
DM_PR:
        MOV  SIG, #1
        MOV  A, DMWIDX
        LCALL GETDIG
        MOV  DPTR, #DIGIT_SEG
        MOVC A, @A+DPTR
        MOV  MASK, A
        MOV  A, DMWIDX

        ADD  A, DMBASE                  ; знакоместо = база + разряд
        MOV  R0, A
        MOV  A, MASK
        MOV  @R0, A
DM_NEXT:
        MOV  A, DMWIDX
        JZ   DM_DONE
        DEC  DMWIDX
        SJMP DM_L

;  Разряды 6..0 (7 цифр) выравниваются по правому краю поля, точка -- на
;  знакоместе разряда единиц рублей (DIGIDX = 2), т.е. ПЕРЕД копейками.
;  Поле затирается ЦЕЛИКОМ, а знакоместо каждой цифры считается от УЖЕ
;  сдвинутой базы (DMBASE = начало поля + ширина - 7), поэтому вызывающая
;  программа не обязана знать ширину: SET_DISPLAY просит ровно FIELD_W
;  знакомест начиная с MODE_CELL+1, и индикатор режима (знакоместо 0) в
;  поле не попадает.  Нули перед числом гасятся, копейки видны всегда.
DRAW_MONEY:
        MOV  A, R0
        ADD  A, R2
        CLR  C
        SUBB A, #7                      ; база = начало поля + ширина - 7
        MOV  DMBASE, A
        MOV  A, R2
        MOV  DMWID, A
        ; --- погасить поле целиком ---
        MOV  A, DMWID
        MOV  R2, A
        MOV  A, R0
        MOV  R0, A
        CLR  A
DM_B:
        MOV  @R0, A
        INC  R0
        DJNZ R2, DM_B
        MOV  DMWIDX, #6                 ; от старшего разряда к младшему: нули
        MOV  SIG, #0                    ; перед числом гасятся, а разряды копеек
DM_L:                                   ; (1 и 0) видны всегда
        MOV  A, DMWIDX
        LCALL GETDIG
        JNZ  DM_PR
        MOV  A, SIG
        JNZ  DM_PR
        MOV  A, DMWIDX
        CJNE A, #2, DM_NEXT             ; разряд единиц рублей виден всегда
DM_PR:
        MOV  SIG, #1
        MOV  A, DMWIDX
        LCALL GETDIG
        MOV  DPTR, #DIGIT_SEG
        MOVC A, @A+DPTR
        MOV  MASK, A
        MOV  A, DMWIDX
        CJNE A, #2, DM_NODP
        MOV  A, MASK
        ORL  A, #SEG_DP                 ; десятичная точка -- перед копейками
        MOV  MASK, A
DM_NODP:
        MOV  A, DMWIDX
        ADD  A, DMBASE                  ; знакоместо = база + разряд
        MOV  R0, A
        MOV  A, MASK
        MOV  @R0, A
DM_NEXT:
        MOV  A, DMWIDX
        JZ   DM_DONE
        DEC  DMWIDX
        SJMP DM_L
DM_DONE:
        RET

        MOV  A, #' '
        LCALL PR_CHAR
PM_NEXT:
        MOV  A, DIGIDX
        JZ   PM_DONE
        DEC  DIGIDX
        SJMP PM_L
PM_DONE:
        RET

;  PR_MONEY_LINE: DPTR = подпись, R1 = BCD, PADN = пробелов до суммы.
;  Сумма занимает 8 колонок и всегда кончается в колонке 31, поэтому вся
;  строка укладывается в 32 колонки из 40 -- иначе рулон (40 колонок)
;  сам разорвал бы строку пополам.  Рядом с PADN стоит РАЗРЯДНОСТЬ суммы,
;  если её печатать не значащими разрядами (R2 != 0); в чеке она не нужна.
PR_MONEY_LINE:
        LCALL PR_STR
        MOV  A, PADN
        LCALL PR_PAD
        MOV  R2, #0
        LCALL PR_MONEY
        LCALL PR_NL
        RET

; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;  ЧЕК
; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;  RECEIPT_HEADER -- напечатать шапку чека.  Это ЕДИНСТВЕННАЯ точка входа,
;  которая печатает шапку: SELFTEST вызывает её для проверки принтера, а
;  KEY_SUMM -- при регистрации первой позиции.  Шапка открывается без
;  ведущих переводов строки: чек начинается с ВЕРХА бумаги, а не после
;  восьми пустых строк.
RECEIPT_HEADER:
        PUSH DPL                        ; DPTR вызывающей программы (нетто)
        PUSH DPH
        LCALL PR_BEGIN                  ; ППИ -> режим 1 (PA уходит принтеру)
        MOV  DPTR, #S_HEAD
        LCALL PR_STR
        MOV  DPTR, #S_DEMO
        LCALL PR_STR
        MOV  DPTR, #S_NOTE
        LCALL PR_STR
        MOV  DPTR, #S_RULE
        LCALL PR_STR
        MOV  DPTR, #S_ID
        LCALL PR_STR
        MOV  A, REC_N
        LCALL PR_NUM2
        MOV  DPTR, #S_CASH
        LCALL PR_STR
        MOV  DPTR, #S_DATE
        LCALL PR_STR
        LCALL PR_END
        POP  DPH
        POP  DPL
        RET

;  RECEIPT_HEAD -- шапка НАЧАЛА чека: считает чек и печатает шапку.
RECEIPT_HEAD:
        INC  REC_N
        LCALL RECEIPT_HEADER
        RET

;  строка позиции: "NN." + цена + пробел + накопленный итог, РОВНО одна
;  строка без ведущих переводов строки (итог виден и после одной позиции).
PRINT_ITEM:
        LCALL PR_BEGIN
        MOV  A, ITEM_N
        LCALL PR_NUM2
        MOV  A, #'.'
        LCALL PR_CHAR
        MOV  R1, #ENTRY
        MOV  PADN, #0                   ; сумма начинается в колонке 4...
PRINT_ITEM_1:
        MOV  A, PADN
        CJNE A, #4, PRINT_ITEM_2
        SJMP PRINT_ITEM_3
PRINT_ITEM_2:
        MOV  A, #' '
        LCALL PR_CHAR
        INC  PADN
        SJMP PRINT_ITEM_1
PRINT_ITEM_3:
        MOV  R1, #ENTRY
        LCALL PR_MONEY                  ; ...цена: 8 колонок, до колонки 11
        MOV  A, #' '
        LCALL PR_CHAR
        MOV  R1, #TOTAL
        LCALL PR_MONEY                  ; итог: колонки 13..20
        LCALL PR_END
        RET
","old_string":";  PR_NUM2: A -> две десятичные цифры
PR_NUM2:
        MOV  B, #10
        DIV  AB
        ADD  A, #'0'
        LCALL PR_CHAR
        MOV  A, B
        ADD  A, #'0'
        LCALL PR_CHAR
        RET

;  PR_PAD: A = число пробелов
PR_PAD:
        MOV  R2, A
        MOV  A, R2
        JZ   PP_DONE
PP_L:
        MOV  A, #' '
        LCALL PR_CHAR
        DJNZ R2, PP_L
PP_DONE:
        RET

;  PR_MONEY: R1 = 4 байта BCD; печатает 8 колонок "99999.99"
PR_MONEY:
        MOV  SIG, #0
        MOV  DIGIDX, #6
PM_L:
        MOV  A, DIGIDX
        LCALL GETDIG
        MOV  DIGIT, A
        MOV  A, DIGIDX
        CJNE A, #1, PM_NODOT            ; точка -- ПЕРЕД копейками
        MOV  A, #'.'
        LCALL PR_CHAR
PM_NODOT:
        MOV  A, DIGIT
        JNZ  PM_PR
        MOV  A, SIG
        JNZ  PM_PR
        MOV  A, DIGIDX
        CJNE A, #2, PM_MAYBE
        SJMP PM_PR
PM_MAYBE:
        CJNE A, #0, PM_SPACE
PM_PR:
        MOV  SIG, #1
        MOV  A, DIGIT
        ADD  A, #'0'
        LCALL PR_CHAR
        SJMP PM_NEXT
PM_SPACE:
        MOV  A, #' '
        LCALL PR_CHAR
PM_NEXT:
        MOV  A, DIGIDX
        JZ   PM_DONE
        DEC  DIGIDX
        SJMP PM_L
PM_DONE:
        RET

;  PR_MONEY_LINE: DPTR = подпись, R1 = BCD, PADN = пробелов до суммы
PR_MONEY_LINE:
        LCALL PR_STR
        MOV  A, PADN
        LCALL PR_PAD
        LCALL PR_MONEY
        LCALL PR_NL
        RET

; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;  ЧЕК
; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
RECEIPT_HEAD:
        LCALL PR_BEGIN
        INC  REC_N
        MOV  DPTR, #S_HEAD
        LCALL PR_STR
        MOV  DPTR, #S_DEMO
        LCALL PR_STR
        MOV  DPTR, #S_NOTE
        LCALL PR_STR
        MOV  DPTR, #S_RULE
        LCALL PR_STR
        MOV  DPTR, #S_ID
        LCALL PR_STR
        MOV  A, REC_N
        LCALL PR_NUM2
        MOV  DPTR, #S_CASH
        LCALL PR_STR
        MOV  DPTR, #S_DATE
        LCALL PR_STR
        LCALL PR_END
        RET

;  строка позиции: "NN. <цена(8)> <итог(8)>"
PRINT_ITEM:
        LCALL PR_BEGIN
        LCALL PR_NL
        MOV  A, ITEM_N
        LCALL PR_NUM2
        MOV  A, #'.'
        LCALL PR_CHAR
        MOV  R1, #ENTRY
        LCALL PR_MONEY
        MOV  A, #' '
        LCALL PR_CHAR
        MOV  R1, #TOTAL
        LCALL PR_MONEY
        LCALL PR_END
        RET
"}

Lead: IMPORTANT — I edited `firmware/demo/cashier.asm` myself while you were diagnosing. Re-read the file before writing; do NOT revert my three edits. They are verified correct against the real board:

Digits 7 8 9 / 4 5 6 / 1 2 3 sit in cols 0..2 (unchanged); the action keys and `00`/`.` were what moved. Before this fix `СУММА` and `ОПЛ` were unreachable.

- The 3 you already knew: `test_intel_hex_output_is_loadable` (assert `:04`/variable-length records, not `:10`), `test_no_acall_in_the_demo` (obsolete — the core now decodes ACALL; delete it or invert it into a positive ACALL test), `test_receipt_reaches_the_board_printer`.

Python includes numpy, pandas, python-docx, python-pptx, openpyxl, Pillow, lxml, and XlsxWriter. Use these libraries for Office files unless the user or workspace instructions select another environment. When Node.js and pnpm paths are returned, run pnpm with that Node executable and pnpm script path. This does not change PATH or package-manager settings.

tools.description: Declare existing files as final deliverables for the user. Use it when the user needs a separate file, especially Office documents, spreadsheets, and slide decks; prefer your final response when that suffices. The user opens the current files; their contents are not copied.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

Lead: resume — your last turn ended without finishing. Two things to correct in your brief, plus a verified status report.

**Correction 1 — my `500.00` expectation was likely WRONG, do not code to it.** Your own firmware comment says «Копейки -- две последние цифры (как в реальной кассе)», i.e. digits typed in are the raw 7-digit field and the last two are kopecks. So `5`,`0`,`0` → value 500 in a `99999.99` field → `00005.00`, which is **5 rubles 00 kopecks**, i.e. `5.00`. My earlier "should be 500.00" was an assumption, not evidence. Derive the correct rendering from `docs/board_contract.md` (8 digits, `DISPLAY_DIGITS = 8`) plus your own `MODE_CELL`/`FIELD_W`/`DIGITS` comments, then pin it with tests — do not encode my guess.

**Correction 2 — cell layout.** `DISPLAY_COLS = 8`, cell 0 = mode indicator, cells 1..7 = 7 money digits with the decimal point as a *segment* on one of those cells (not a separate cell). Currently after `5`,`0`,`0` the board reports `'005    0'` — left-ish aligned with a stray `0` in cell 7 and the mode cell consumed by a digit. After your fix it must be right-aligned in cells 1..7 with cell 0 holding the mode glyph only.

**Verified status (I ran it just now):**
- UI end-to-end chain works: invoking the `СУММА` **button** → demo firmware → board printer produced **receipt 0 → 9 lines**. So keyboard wiring, BCD entry, KEYMAP and the printer path are all good.
- Boot display `'000    0'`, after 5,0,0 `'005    0'`, after `СУММА` `'000    0'`.
- Receipt still has 8 leading blank lines (first non-empty is line 9) — your bug #2.
- `tests/test_demo_firmware.py` is the only red suite: 11 failures. Everything else in the project is green (cpu 52, board 64, ui 38, recover 7).

**Please finish**: fix DRAW_MONEY cell placement + the printer leading blank lines, then make all 11 tests green (`python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py"`), including the 7 `TestDemoOnMockBus` tests and `test_keymap_table_matches_python_layout` which still assert the old keymap — those must be updated to the board coordinates I sent earlier:
```
DB 7,8,9,K_X,K_SUMM,K_PAY,K_ITOG,K_00
DB 4,5,6,K_NONE,K_CANCEL,K_NONE,K_SUB,K_DOT
DB 1,2,3,K_NONE,K_NONE,K_NONE,K_ENTER,K_CLEAR
DB 0,K_NONE,K_NONE,K_NONE,K_NONE,K_NONE,K_NONE,K_NONE
```
Also fix `test_intel_hex_output_is_loadable` (accept variable-length records) and delete/invert `test_no_acall_in_the_demo` (core implements ACALL now).

Reply with before/after display strings and a green test run. Work in `firmware/demo/**` and `tests/test_demo_firmware.py` only.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.
